Prealgebra · Lesson 12.4

Work Backwards

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Some problems hand you the ending and ask for the beginning. You get the final amount, or the last term, or the state after every step, and the starting value is the missing piece. Guessing a start and pushing it forward is slow. The stronger move is to stand at the ending and rewind, undoing one step at a time until you reach the start. This last lesson of the course is about that rewind.

Problem
A number trick goes like this. Think of a number, double it, then add 99. Priya follows the steps and lands on 4141. What number did she think of?
Show a hint
  • Undo the steps from the end. The last thing done was adding 99, so the first undo is subtracting 99.
Show the full solution

Undo the add 99 first, 41−9=3241−9=32. Then undo the doubling, 32÷2=1632÷2=16​.

Check it forward, 1616 doubled is 3232, and 32+9=4132+9=41.

Problem
Another trick has three steps. Subtract 44, multiply by 55, then add 77. Marcus finishes on 5252. What number did he start with?
Show a hint
  • Peel the steps in reverse order. The add 77 came last, so it is undone first, then the multiply, then the subtract.
  • Each undo swaps the operation for its opposite. Adding becomes subtracting, multiplying becomes dividing.
Show the full solution

Undo the add 77, 52−7=4552−7=45. Undo the multiply by 55, 45÷5=945÷5=9. Undo the subtract 44, 9+4=139+4=13​.

Forward, 13−4=913−4=9, times 55 is 4545, plus 77 is 5252.

Key idea
Undo in reverse order. Undoing a chain of operations has two rules. Each operation becomes its opposite, so adding becomes subtracting and multiplying becomes dividing. The order reverses too, so the last step forward is the first one undone. Forgetting to reverse the order is the common mistake. The diagram shows the chain forward, then undone.
Problem
Theo bought a rare trading card. He later sold it to Uma, taking a loss of 55 tokens. Uma then sold it to Vik for 3232 tokens, making a profit of 88 tokens on her purchase. How many tokens did Theo originally pay?
Show a hint
  • Start at the end. Uma sold for 3232 with a profit of 88, so what she paid comes from undoing that profit.
  • What Uma paid is exactly what Theo received. Undo Theo's loss of 55 from there.
Show the full solution

Uma sold for 3232 at a profit of 88, so she paid 32−8=2432−8=24. That 2424 is what Theo got for the card, and it left him down 55, so he paid 24+5=2924+5=29​.

A seller with a profit paid less than the sale price, so undoing a profit subtracts and undoing a loss adds.

Problem
A rain barrel goes through the same routine each day. It loses half its water to the garden, and then the gardener pours 66 liters back in. After two full days of this, the barrel holds 2121 liters. How many liters did it hold at the start?
Show a hint
  • Rewind day two first. Undo the 66-liter pour, then undo the halving by doubling.
  • That gives the level after day one, and the same two undos again reach the start.
Show the full solution

Rewind day two. Before the 66 liters went in the barrel held 21−6=1521−6=15, and before losing half it held 3030. So day one ended at 3030.

Rewind day one the same way, 30−6=2430−6=24, then double to get 4848​.

Inside each day the pour happens last, so it is the first thing you undo.

Key idea
Undo a multi-day routine one day at a time. A routine repeated over several days is one long chain of operations. Undo the days in reverse order, and undo the steps inside each day in reverse order too, so the pour is undone before the halving. Then run your answer forward through the routine. If it matches the given ending, the answer is right.
after losing halfafter adding 6
day 12430
day 21521
Problem
A sourdough starter doubles in size every day, and it completely fills its jar on day 1010. On which day was the jar exactly one quarter full?
Show a hint
  • Run the doubling backward. One day earlier the jar was half full.
  • One quarter is half of half.
Show the full solution

Working back from day 1010, day 99 held half a jar, and day 88 held half of that, which is one quarter.

88​

Day 1010 is the only amount you are given, so stepping backward from it beats hunting for the starting size.

Problem
In a certain list, every number is the sum of the two numbers just before it. The list ends with …,  a,  b,  19,  31,  50…,a,b,19,31,50. Find the value of aa.
Show a hint
  • The rule runs forward as addition, so it rewinds as subtraction. The number before 1919 and 3131 satisfies b+19=31b+19=31.
  • Once bb is known, the same subtraction one step earlier finds aa.
Show the full solution

Each number is the sum of the two before it, so b+19=31b+19=31, giving b=12b=12. One step earlier, a+12=19a+12=19, so a=7a=7​.

Forward, the list reads 7,12,19,31,507,12,19,31,50, and each term is the sum of the two before it.

Problem
A bacteria colony in a dish triples every hour. At 55 in the afternoon the dish holds 405405 colonies. How many colonies did it hold at 11 in the afternoon?
Show a hint
  • Four hours separate the two clock times, so rewind four triplings.
  • Each rewind divides by 33.
Show the full solution

Rewinding one hour divides by 33, and four hours pass between 11 and 55.

405÷3÷3÷3÷3=405÷81=5405÷3÷3÷3÷3=405÷81=5​

Forward check, 5,15,45,135,4055,15,45,135,405, one tripling per hour.

Key idea
Undo the rule that generated the sequence. Growth processes and sequences follow a rule, so rebuild them from the ending by inverting that rule. Doubling is undone by halving, tripling by dividing by three, and a term made by adding the two before it is undone by a subtraction. Start at the last known value and step backward, one inverse per step, writing each recovered value into its real position. This is also why a jar that fills on day ten is only a quarter full on day eight, since most of the growth happens in the last few steps. When you are done, run the chain forward, and if you get the given ending back, the values are correct.
Fun fact
Working backwards has a long history. Chess players study endgames by starting from checkmate and stepping in reverse, a method called retrograde analysis. Maze designers know their puzzles fall fastest to solvers who begin at the exit. And escape-room writers plot the final door first, then build the clues backward toward the entrance.
Problem
Two juice pitchers sit on a counter. First, pitcher A pours into pitcher B exactly as much juice as B already contains, doubling B. Then pitcher B pours into pitcher A exactly as much as A contains at that moment, doubling A. Now each pitcher holds 3636 centiliters. How many centiliters did pitcher A hold at the start?
Show a hint
  • Undo the second pour first. It doubled A to 3636, so before it A held 1818, and the poured amount came out of B.
  • Then undo the first pour, which had doubled B. Half of B's amount at that moment had come from A.
Show the full solution

Rewind the second pour. It doubled A to 3636, so A held 1818 before it, and the 1818 that arrived came from B, which held 36+18=5436+18=54.

Rewind the first pour. It doubled B to 5454, so B held 2727, and that 2727 came from A, which started with 18+27=4518+27=45​.

Forward, 4545 and 2727 become 1818 and 5454, then 3636 and 3636.

Problem
On a game show, a contestant spends half of her tokens in round one, then pays a 77-token entry fee for round two. In round two she spends half of what she has left, then pays a 33-token exit fee. She walks away with 1111 tokens. How many tokens did she start with?
Show a hint
  • Rewind the four events in reverse. Undo the exit fee, undo the round-two halving, undo the entry fee, undo the round-one halving.
  • Undoing a fee means adding it back, and undoing a halving means doubling.
Show the full solution

Rewind from 1111. Add back the exit fee to get 1414, double to get 2828, add back the entry fee to get 3535, and double again to get 7070​.

Forward, half of 7070 leaves 3535, the entry fee leaves 2828, half leaves 1414, and the exit fee leaves 1111.

Key idea
Working backwards, and the four strategies together. Work backwards when you know the ending and the beginning is missing. Reverse every operation, reverse the order, then run your answer forward to check it. That is the fourth strategy of the chapter. Patterns turn a large position into a short division, organized lists count every case without missing one, pictures show the structure of a word problem, and working backwards recovers a starting value from a final one. Prealgebra ends here. These four are the strategies to try when a problem is unfamiliar.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A number is multiplied by 44, then 99 is subtracted, giving 3939. What was the number?
Show the solution

Adding back the 99 gives 4848, and dividing by 44 gives 1212​. Forward, 12×4−9=3912×4−9=39.

Practice
A number has 88 added to it, the result is divided by 33, and that result is multiplied by 55, giving 4545. What was the original number?
Show the solution

From 4545, dividing by 55 gives 99, multiplying by 33 gives 2727, and subtracting 88 gives 1919​. Forward, (19+8)÷3×5=45(19+8)÷3×5=45.

Practice
Rosa bought a bicycle and later sold it to Sam at a 1212-token profit. Sam then sold it for 8787 tokens, taking a 99-token loss. How many tokens did Rosa pay for the bicycle?
Show the solution

Sam paid 87+9=9687+9=96. Rosa received that 9696 at a 1212-token profit, so she had paid 96−12=8496−12=84​.

Practice
A candy jar is visited by two siblings, one after the other. Each takes half the candies in the jar and then, feeling guilty, puts 22 back. After both visits the jar holds 1414 candies. How many were in the jar before the first visit?
Show the solution

Rewind the second sibling, 14−2=1214−2=12, and doubling gives 2424. Rewind the first, 24−2=2224−2=22, and doubling gives 4444​.

Forward, 44→22+2=24→12+2=1444→22+2=24→12+2=14.

Practice
A video's view count doubles every day. On Friday it reaches 96,00096,000 views. How many days earlier did it stand at 12,00012,000 views?
Show the solution

Backward, 96,000→48,000→24,000→12,00096,000→48,000→24,000→12,000, three halvings, so 33​ days earlier.

Practice
In a list where every number is the sum of the two before it, the final three numbers are 13,21,3413,21,34. What number sits four places before the 3434?
Show the solution

Rewinding, before 1313 sits 21−13=821−13=8, and before that sits 13−8=513−8=5. The list runs 5,8,13,21,345,8,13,21,34, and four places before the 3434 is 55​.

Practice
A stamp collection's value has tripled twice over the years and now stands at 486486 tokens. What was its value before either tripling?
Show the solution

Two rewinds give 486÷3=162486÷3=162 and 162÷3=54162÷3=54​.

Practice
A car enters a parking garage on some level, drives up 55 levels, down 88, and up 22, ending on level 66. On which level did it enter?
Show the solution

Undo the moves in reverse, 6−2=46−2=4, then 4+8=124+8=12, then 12−5=712−5=7​.

Forward, 7+5−8+2=67+5−8+2=6.

Practice
After giving away half of his stickers and then 44 more, Leo has 2626 stickers left. How many did he start with?
Show the solution

Adding the 44 back gives 3030, and doubling gives 6060​. Forward, half of 6060 is 3030, minus 44 is 2626.

Practice
Four integers form a chain in which each number after the first is twice the previous number minus 11. The fourth number is 4141. What is the first?
Show the solution

Rewinding one link means adding 11 and halving. From 4141, the third number is (41+1)÷2=21(41+1)÷2=21, the second is (21+1)÷2=11(21+1)÷2=11, and the first is (11+1)÷2=6(11+1)÷2=6​.

Forward, 6→11→21→416→11→21→41.
